title: boardsmith.json
description: Single source of truth for the set of top-level keys a boardsmith.json project config may legitimately carry. `src/cli/lib/config-schema.ts` derives ALLOWED_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS from `Object.keys(properties)` below, and `boardsmith validate` / `boardsmith dev` startup use that list to reject unknown/misspelled keys with a did-you-mean suggestion. Do NOT add a key here unless it has a real read site: either a command in src/cli/commands consumes it (see the file:line trace in 135-05-PLAN.md's read_first), or the PUBLISHING PLATFORM consumes it out of the manifest that build.ts's deriveManifest produces by spreading this config. The platform has two manifest sinks, and reaching either one takes MORE than listing a key here. (1) The Convex sink, which is what the platform's lobby and game pages are read from: `convex/publish.ts` `initiatePublishServer` stores verbatim what it is SENT, but what it is sent is an allow-list projection built by `buildInitiateManifest` in `src/cli/lib/publish-api.ts` — a key absent from that function never arrives, silently, however well it is declared here. (2) The R2 sink the runtime session host reads: the bundle zip carries `dist/manifest.json` whole, and the games worker rebuilds an R2 copy through its own allowlist (`games/src/manifest-schema.ts`), silently dropping keys that allowlist does not name. So a key needs a named reader on at least one sink AND a place on that sink's forwarding list; a key only the Convex sink carries is invisible to the runtime session host by design. EVERY property below therefore carries a REQUIRED `x-convex-sink` boolean saying whether sink (1) consumes it AS A TOP-LEVEL KEY. A key marked false is not necessarily invisible to the platform: what a bundle can do reaches it inside the DERIVED `capabilities` object that `build.ts` resolves (#171) and `publish-api.ts` forwards explicitly, exactly as `playerCount` is forwarded, and a derived key is not an authorable property so it is not listed here at all. `config-schema.ts` derives CONVEX_SINK_KEYS from it and `buildInitiateManifest` forwards exactly that set, so `marked true but not forwarded` cannot be written; `validate.test.ts` refuses a property that declares neither, so `added and never decided` cannot be committed. Sink (2)'s allowlist lives in another repository and is NOT expressible here — do not add a second annotation claiming to govern it.

$schema.description: Optional editor schema reference (point it at this file's $id for IDE autocomplete/validation). Ignored by the CLI — this is the one key exempt from the read-site rule above, because the schema itself can only be consumed through it.

backend.description: WHICH BACKEND RUNS THIS GAME, and the only place it is declared. `table` holds the whole element tree resident, snapshots per action, and keeps history, undo, bots and spectators; `world` keeps only named partitions resident, checkpoints what a command dirtied, and runs continuously. Same engine, same element tree, same action system, different storage and checkpoint policy. Required, because a default would be a backend nobody chose. It is declared HERE rather than derived from the compiled rules because `boardsmith dev` has to know which host to start before it loads any rules -- but a declaration that contradicts the code is refused: `boardsmith build` and `boardsmith validate` both check it against `gameDefinition.world` (see src/session/capabilities.ts). What the choice IMPLIES is not written here or anywhere else by hand: build resolves it into the manifest's `capabilities` object, and every reader -- the shell, the CLI, the publishing platform -- reads that object rather than this name.

audience.description: Who the game is for — exactly one platform shelf. The canonical value list lives on the platform (GET /api/taxonomy); `boardsmith publish` preflight-validates against it. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

tags.description: Freeform discovery tags (mechanisms, themes, eras) — e.g. 'abstract', 'worker-placement', 'family-friendly'. Normalized server-side. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

playtime.description: Estimated play time range in minutes (min <= max). Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

cooperative.description: True when players win or lose together. A structural fact synced to the platform on every publish. Scaffold-emitted; shape-checked by validate.ts.

thumbnail.description: Relative path to the game's thumbnail image, resolved from the project root. NOT scaffold-emitted: `boardsmith new` creates no thumbnail image, so declaring the key by default meant every new game named a file its bundle did not carry. `boardsmith validate` fails when a declared asset path resolves to nothing (`x-asset-path` marks which keys it checks).

backdrop.description: The game's cover backdrop: atmospheric art with no text, exactly 1500 x 500, a JPEG or WebP of at most 400 KB (409,600 bytes). A path relative to the project root. `boardsmith build` copies the file into the bundle at that same path and writes the path, normalised, into the manifest, where the publishing platform reads it from the R2 sink and makes every smaller size itself. `boardsmith validate` checks the format, size and transparency from the file's header, against `src/cli/lib/cover-art.ts`, which mirrors ShufflewickPub's game art spec. Optional: a game with none shows the platform's placeholder (#1630).

logo.description: The game's logo: its wordmark centred on a transparent square, exactly 1500 x 1500, a PNG with an alpha channel of at most 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). A path relative to the project root. `boardsmith build` copies the file into the bundle at that same path and writes the path, normalised, into the manifest, where the publishing platform reads it from the R2 sink and makes every smaller size itself. `boardsmith validate` checks the format, size and transparency from the file's header, against `src/cli/lib/cover-art.ts`, which mirrors ShufflewickPub's game art spec. Optional: a game with none shows the platform's placeholder (#1630).

box.description: A render of the game's box: exactly 280 x 280, a PNG with an alpha channel of at most 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). A path relative to the project root. `boardsmith build` copies the file into the bundle at that same path and writes the path, normalised, into the manifest, where the publishing platform reads it from the R2 sink and makes every smaller size itself. `boardsmith validate` checks the format, size and transparency from the file's header, against `src/cli/lib/cover-art.ts`, which mirrors ShufflewickPub's game art spec. Optional: a game with none shows the platform's placeholder (#1630).

gameOptions.description: THE ONE DECLARATION OF THE GAME'S OPTIONS (#701): a gameDefinition that declares gameOptions is refused. Each entry is an option with an id, the name the game reads it by (options.<id>), and a default, which every host fills in when nobody chose the option (selectGameOptions, the start op, createTestGame), so a game never repeats a default in code. The dev host, boardsmith simulate and createTestGame read this list; every BoardSmith command attaches it to the loaded gameDefinition, and boardsmith build writes it into the published rules, so the start op fills every option the host did not pass. boardsmith build copies it into the manifest the platform's lobby lists, leaving out every designerOnly option: a designer's knob that only boardsmith simulate and the dev host set, and that every real game plays at its default.

playerOptions.description: Per-player option definitions surfaced in the dev host and lobby. Read by dev.ts.

colorPalette.description: Custom per-player color choices. Read by dev.ts.

paths.description: Optional overrides for the rules/ui source directories (paths.rules, paths.ui). Read by build.ts, dev.ts, simulate.ts, validate.ts, evolve-bot-weights.ts.

agents.description: Which Claude Code agent type the bs- skills dispatch each role as, when not BoardSmith's own bs-<role> agent. The roles are mechanical (bulk edits, search, summaries), bounded (implementation where failing tests define done), judgement (spec, investigate, red team, fidelity, anything touching a ruling) review (the review that runs once boardsmith verify has passed) and second-opinion (an independent second reading, which must not resolve to the same agent type as judgement). A role left out is dispatched as its bs- default, which `boardsmith claude` installs. Read by `boardsmith agent`; never published: the build leaves it out of manifest.json.

mutation.description: An override of how many mutants `boardsmith mutate` runs at once (trials), and the total Vitest test workers they share (workers, at least trials). The unmutated run gets all the workers, each trial workers / trials, rounded down. Without it, every sampled mutant runs at once. Read by mutate.ts (`lib/mutation-budget.ts`); never published.

publisher.description: Publisher slug, written back into boardsmith.json by `boardsmith publish` (from --publisher). Read by publish.ts.

platforms.description: The ids each publishing platform gave this game, written back by `boardsmith publish` after a publish to that platform and read only by a publish to the same one: dev and prod are separate deployments with separate ids (#704). Read by publish.ts.

defaultTimePerTurn.description: The time per turn a new table of this game starts with (#1830). The table may choose another from the same set until the game starts. The host runs the only clock: when a step declared `timed: true` is open, it closes the step at the end of the table's time per turn by submitting `idleAction` for every seat still due, and sends that deadline to every screen. Leave it out for five minutes. Read by the platform's lobby and by `boardsmith dev`, which times every timed step with it; `boardsmith validate` and `boardsmith build` refuse a value outside the set (`src/session/time-per-turn.ts`).

maxWatchSeconds.description: The longest watch time, in seconds, any step of this game can report with `timed: { watchSeconds }` (#1831), such as a battle replay everyone watches before they can act. The host sets a timed step's deadline to turn start + min(the step's watch time, this) + the table's time per turn, and tells screens when the watching ends, so a buggy or hostile bundle cannot hold a table still past it. 1 to 300. Declare it exactly when a step reports watch time: `boardsmith validate` and `boardsmith build` refuse it when no step reports watch time, and refuse a step that reports watch time without it when that step is in the first table they find a timed step in (`src/session/time-per-turn.ts`).

idleAction.description: The action the platform submits on behalf of a seat whose round deadline expired, for a game that ships no bot. Required by the platform alongside `roundDeadline` when the bundle ships no bot. Whether it does is not authorable: `boardsmith build` derives it from the compiled `gameDefinition.bot` and sends it as `capabilities.bots`. Also required whenever a flow step is declared `timed: true`: the host closes a timed step by submitting this action for every seat that has not acted, never by handing the seat to a bot, so `boardsmith validate` and `boardsmith build` refuse a timed game without it (`capabilities.timedSteps`). Consumed by the platform (manifest-schema.ts `idleAction`).

imageSources.description: Where this game's artwork may be loaded from besides its own bundle. A published bundle's HTML is served under `img-src 'self' data:`, so a game whose artwork lives in a separate repository shows no pictures at all unless it declares the origins here. Each entry is an https:// origin ("https://cdn.example.com") or an origin and a path PREFIX ending in a slash ("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/owner/art/abc123/"), which pins one directory at one commit rather than opening a whole host. Images only: scripts, styles, fonts, connections and form targets stay exactly as bounded as they were. Consumed by the platform (manifest-schema.ts `imageSources`), which validates the same shape at upload and writes the entries into the served Content-Security-Policy.

defaultHours.description: Used by a table that expresses no preference. Must satisfy minHours <= defaultHours <= maxHours.

minHours.description: Floor a table may choose. The platform's own floor is 1 hour.

maxHours.description: Ceiling a table may choose. The platform's own ceiling is 720 hours (30 days).

mindingSafe.description: The author's explicit acknowledgement that a caretaker bot may play an absent player's seat in THIS game. The platform requires it when the bundle's own bot resolves an expiry, which is what `capabilities.bots` reports.

roundDeadline.description: How long one round may sit before the platform intervenes. Consumed by the platform (manifest-schema.ts `roundDeadline`), which also enforces its own hour bounds and requires either a bot in the bundle (reported as `capabilities.bots`, derived from the compiled `gameDefinition.bot`) or an `idleAction` alongside it.

gameId.description: Stable game identifier on this platform.

publisherId.description: Stable identifier, on this platform, of the publisher that owns the game.

name.description: The action name, exactly as the game's rules register it.

args.description: Optional literal arguments submitted with the action. Opaque to the platform — what constitutes a legal action is the game's business.

namedAction.description: An action the PLATFORM submits on a game's behalf, named as the game's rules register it.
